title: Eastern Front
summary: The German-Soviet theatre of World War II began when Nazi Germany and its allies invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941. After German advances stalled before Moscow, Soviet forces pushed back and took Berlin in spring 1945; Germany's forces in the east surrendered on 9 May 1945. It was the largest and deadliest theatre of the war.

uncertainty.note: Start is the invasion date; end is the German surrender in the east per USHMM.

where.modern_name: Moscow, Russia (proxy pin; the front spanned eastern Europe)
where.historical_name: Eastern Europe, Soviet Union and German-held territories; pin at Moscow, capital of the USSR (proxy)

importance.justification: Described by the US Holocaust Memorial Museum as the largest and deadliest theatre of World War II.

audience_note: Includes mass killing of civilians, the shooting of Jews by Einsatzgruppen, and the deaths of Soviet prisoners of war.
